question: The amount of Cash Reserves that commercial banks are required to keep with the RBI is referred to as:
solution:
The correct answer is __**CRR**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **amount of cash reserves that commercial banks are required to keep with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is called the Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR)**
 
• The percentage of cash required to be kept in reserves as against the bank's total deposits, is called the **Cash Reserve Ratio**. 
 
• The cash reserve is either stored in the bank’s vault or is sent to the** RBI**.
 
• Banks can’t lend the** CRR money** to corporates or individual borrowers, banks can’t use that money for investment purposes. And Banks don’t earn any interest on that money.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Repo rate**

 
 
• The** rate at which commercial banks borrow money from the RBI. **
 
• The RBI changes the repo rate based on macroeconomic factors. 
 
• Lower repo rates can help the economy grow and reduce inflation. 
 
 
 
• **SLR** 
 
 
• The** percentage of deposits that commercial banks must keep as liquid asset**s.
 
• Liquid assets include cash, gold, and government securities.
 
• The RBI sets the SLR rate.
 
 
 
• **Bank rate** 
 
 
• Bank rate** is a rate at which the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) provides t**he loan to commercial banks without keeping any security.
 
• There is** no agreement on repurchase that will be drawn up or agreed upon with no collateral as well. **
